newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end higher after a strong auction.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end higher after a strong auction.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Thursday's Tokyo session up after a strong 10-year JGB auction, but pared gains somewhat on profit taking fueled in part by a stock market tumble, traders said.
The March contract closed up 0.15 at 124.95 after rising as high as 125.26. Volume was 45,214 contracts.
The auction for the 2.7 percent 10-year JGB produced a lowest price of 100.50, Japan's Finance Ministry said.
The Tokyo stock market's sharp drop was partly to blame for profit taking before the close, traders said. The Nikkei 225 average ended off 606.51 points or 3.25 percent at 18,073.87.
"People were not overly worried about stocks for much of the day, but after seeing the Nikkei extending losses in late trade, players became a bit more cautious," a brokerage house trader said.

Added a trader at a city bank's securities unit, "Buying emerged in the early afternoon on expectations of a good auction result, but after the announcement some dealers moved to liquidate long positions."
Players had expected the auction to produce a lowest price of around 100.35, traders said.

Despite today's JGB gains, traders said more falls in Tokyo shares may spur some investors to take profits on JGBs to cover stock losses ahead of the fiscal year-end in March, but the proceeds would probably be reinvested in bonds eventually.
"If the Nikkei slides sharply below 18,000 tomorrow, worries of 'triple weakness' in the yen, stocks and bonds may emerge again," one trader said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.505 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd and Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd said on Thursday that they would leave their long-term prime lending rates for January unchanged at a record low 2.5 percent.
NCB and LTCB also said they would leave the coupon rates on their January five-year debentures, sold to institutional investors, unchanged at 2.15 percent and 1.8 percent respectively.
NCB left the coupon unchanged despite a sharp deviation between the December debenture coupon and its secondary market yield.

NCB's December debenture was trading at a yield of around 3.06 to 3.07 percent in the secondary market on Wednesday, about 90 basis points above its coupon. No transactions were seen today, traders said.
